input.rationale: Governing law is acceptable at the preferred level: Section 15.5 (p0627), mirrored in the Letter Agreement (p0671), applies New York law. The dispute forum, however, fails both preferred and fallback: Section 15.6(a) sends all merits Disputes to mandatory, confidential JAMS arbitration with the seat redacted ([***]), rather than to the state and federal courts in New York County (preferred) or Delaware, California or London courts (fallback); the only judicial routes preserved are enforcement of the award, the IP-registration carve-out in 15.6(h) and interim relief in 15.6(j). We therefore replaced the arbitration referral with exclusive New York County court jurisdiction over the merits, switched off the arbitral machinery in 15.6(b)-(e), and conformed 15.6 (a) language, (f), (g) and (j) so no arbitration mechanic dangles; the customary interim injunctive-relief carve-out is preserved and does not defeat exclusivity. The retained 15.6(h) carve-out for patent/trademark validity in the granting country and 15.6(i) invention-ownership adjudication are left intact as customary IP-specific mechanics and are noted rather than redlined.

mappings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York without reference to any rules of conflict of laws.

mappings.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.

proposal.summary: Route Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County instead of JAMS arbitration in an undisclosed seat, and conform the remaining dispute-resolution mechanics.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law is agreed, but our position requires the merits to be decided by courts rather than by arbitration in an undisclosed seat, so we have submitted Disputes to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County and switched off the arbitral machinery. We have kept the interim injunctive-relief carve-out, the punitive-damages waiver and the stay of termination during a pending proceeding, conformed only to the new court forum.
